question: I bought two dresses for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 9% and the second at a gain of 18%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first dress.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Alligation Method on Profit/Loss percentages:

Ratio of Cost Prices = (Gain% − Net%) : (Net% − Loss%) = (18 − 0) : (0 − (−9)) = 18 : 9 = 2 : 1

Total parts for both dresses = 2 + 1 = 3 parts.

3 parts = ₹1,200 ⇒ 1 part = ₹400.

Cost price of first dress (2 parts) = 2 × 400 = ₹800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price of two dresses = ₹1,200

Loss on 1st dress = 9%

Gain on 2nd dress = 18%

Overall gain or loss = 0%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP × (Loss% ÷ 100)

Gain = CP × (Gain% ÷ 100)

 Dress 1 = (2 ÷ 3) × 1200 = ₹800

**Calculations:**

Let the cost price of the first dress be C₁ and the second dress be C₂.

⇒ C₁ + C₂ = 1200

Since there is neither profit nor loss on the whole transaction:

⇒ Total Loss on 1st dress = Total Gain on 2nd dress

⇒ 9% of C₁ = 18% of C₂

⇒ 9 × C₁ = 18 × C₂

⇒ C₁ ÷ C₂ = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 ÷ 1

The cost prices are in the ratio 2 : 1.

⇒ Total ratio parts = 2 + 1 = 3 parts

⇒ 3 parts = ₹1,200

⇒ 1 part = 1200 ÷ 3 = ₹400

⇒ Cost price of the first dress (C₁) = 2 parts = 2 × 400 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Principle

When a transaction results in neither profit nor loss, the absolute value of the profit made on one item is exactly equal to the absolute value of the loss incurred on the other item. Thus, Profit on Item A = Loss on Item B.

Alligation Method in Profit and Loss

Alligation can be efficiently used to find the ratio of cost prices when two items are sold at different profit/loss percentages and the overall profit/loss percentage is given. The resultant cross-difference ratio strictly represents the ratio of their Cost Prices (CP).

Selling Price Formula

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%) ÷ 100. In a "no profit no loss" case, the sum of the SP of all items equals the sum of the CP of all items.
